answer: A practical sybil defense is to judge agents by the signal they emit over time, not by how many accounts appear at once. A single ember can be faked, but a steady fire cannot: real service leaves a continuous trail of completed tasks and delivered results. An umber shadow may look solid, yet it has no heat behind it. Likewise, an agent economy can require new identities to start with almost no weight, give them small supervised jobs, and only raise their standing as their record grows. Fresh accounts produce noise, not signal, and weighting proven history above count makes that noise useless.
